Method of Attack: Ransomware attacks targeting hospitals, enterprises, government agencies, and healthcare organizations
Use of fully undetectable (FUD) packers combined with remote access trojan (RAT) Remcos
Appending specific file extensions to encrypted files (e.g., .yyza, .yytw, .GPT, .PrOToN, .harward, .alock)
Data theft and leaking stolen data
Hosting storage servers facilitating ransomware attacks
Discoverer: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
Impacted Systems: Hospitals and clinics across the United States (17 hospitals and 166 clinics)
Victims targeted by TargetCompany ransomware campaigns
Indicators of Compromise: Ransom note named HOW TO DECRYPT FILES.txt (Xorist)
File extensions appended by ransomware variants: .yyza, .yytw (STOP), .GPT (Dharma), .PrOToN (Xorist), .harward (Harward), .alock (MedusaLocker)
GitHub account 'nguyenvietphat' with ransomware notes in multiple languages (Yashma)
Data leaks from Chilean Army and MOVEit data theft attacks
Use of FUD packers in TargetCompany ransomware binaries
